title: The effect of manual osteopathic treatment on the time at which preterm infants are able to drink sufficient amounts of fluid independently
summary: The point at which a preterm baby is able to drink a sufficient amount of fluid independently is one of the factors that determines, amongst other things, when they are discharged from hospital. Furthermore, this is often the moment when parents are given their first independent and important role in their child’s care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria: Preterm infants from 33 + 0 weeks of gestation (WG) (gestational age, GA), preterm infants, whose parents have signed the consent form.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria: Preterm infants at 33 + 0 weeks’ gestation with a confirmed or suspected underlying genetic condition, underlying cardiovascular condition, underlying neurological/neuromuscular condition, confirmed necrotising enterocolitis, underlying gastrointestinal condition (atresias, strictures, etc.), and preterm infants before and/or after surgery.
